text: In haplodiploid species such as honeybees, a worker is related to her full sisters by a coefficient of r = 0.75, which is higher than her relatedness to her own potential offspring (r = 0.5).
explanation: True. Haplodiploidy produces r = 0.75 among full sisters, closer than any other natural relationship and higher than the r = 0.5 to one's own offspring. By Hamilton's rule (rB > C), this unusually high relatedness helps explain why sterile workers can gain more inclusive fitness by rearing sisters than by reproducing themselves.
